sentences.text: The accused in Crime No. 255/2022 of Ambalathara Police Station, Kasaragod now pending as S.C.No.725/2023 on the file of the Fast Track Sessions Court, Kasaragode, filed this Crl.M.C under Section 482 of Crl.M.C praying for quashing all further proceedings against him.

The offences alleged against the petitioner are under Sections 450, 376(2)(n), 354. 354(D) and 506(i) of IPC.
2.

The prosecution case is that, when the defacto complainant was working as Librarian in TK Sreedharan Library in Belur Village, the accused outraged her modesty, intimidated her and thereafter, on 22.08.2021, during the night trespassed into her bedroom and committed rape upon her.
It is also alleged that, thereafter on 16.12.2021, 17.12.2021 and 04.01.2022, he committed rape upon her.

3. According to the learned counsel for the petitioner, even if the entire allegations leveled against the petitioner are believed as such, the same will not constitute the offences as alleged by the prosecution.
Therefore, he prayed for quashing all further proceedings against the petitioner.
4. The petition was strongly opposed by the learned Public Prosecutor.
Though notice was served on the 3rd respondent/defacto complainant, she did not turn up.
6. On a perusal of the FI Statement it is revealed that the petitioner and the defacto complainant had sexual relationship with each other on several days at different place.
Therefore, primafacie, it is revealed that the relationship between them was a consensual one.
From the FI Statement, it is also revealed that the said relationship continued even while the marriage of the defacto complainant with another person was subsisting.

In the above circumstances, the allegations leveled against the Dileesh T vs State Of Kerala on 25 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28557240/
2 petitioner does not make out the offences as alleged and as such there is no meaning in continuing the proceedings alleged against the petitioner.
